name: Shelf Standard Rain Poncho
description:
A shapeless pull-over poncho in heavy-duty recycled polyurethane, available in grey, olive, and a faded rust-orange. It covers from the crown of the head to mid-thigh, has a single drawstring hood, and two slash pockets that are more or less watertight. The seams are heat-welded rather than sewn. It folds into its own small pouch. On the Shelf, where covered transit is patchy and the lakefront weather comes in fast, this is a survival item as much as a garment.

These are manufactured by several competing Shelf-adjacent micro-operations, all producing nearly identical product at the lowest possible price point. Some are stamped with brand names — Greycoast, Dura-Lo, Westpont Basics — that may or may not represent actual ongoing companies. Quality varies. The orange ones are slightly better-made than the others, according to a persistent Shelf rumor that may or may not have any basis in fact.
what_it_says: You are on the Shelf or close to it. You bought this because you had to. You might be embarrassed by it or you might not care at all.
worn_by: Tier 2 workers in hazardous wet environments
manufacturer: Various Shelf-adjacent micro-manufacturers (Greycoast, Dura-Lo, Westpont Basics)
story_hooks: A body was found wearing one of these — the manufacturing stamp on the inside identifies a specific Shelf block production run, which could pinpoint where the victim lived
Someone has been distributing these to Shelf residents for free, with a small symbol stamped inside each one — nobody knows who or why
A Tier 4 fashion house released a 'deconstructed homage' to this poncho for Φ2,400 and the feeds are furious

physical_description.visual_profile: A formless, utilitarian silhouette that drapes loosely from shoulders to mid-thigh, reading as pure function over form. The poncho creates a tent-like profile that obscures the wearer's body entirely—deliberately anonymous and mass-produced looking. On the Shelf, this reads as survival kit, not fashion.
physical_description.fit: Completely oversized and shapeless—designed to layer over heavy clothing or augmentation rigs without constraint. The drawstring hood cinches at the crown but the body hangs baggy and unrestricted. Mobility is prioritized over silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty recycled polyurethane—dense, chemical-smelling, industrial. Waterproof but plasticky, with a slight sheen that shows dirt and hand oils easily.
physical_description.texture: Smooth but with a subtle granular quality from recycled content. Heat-welded seams create visible ridges that catch light. Slightly stiff when new, becoming more pliable with weathering. Prone to cracking at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominantly grey (most common), olive drab, or faded rust-orange. No patterns. Discoloration and watermarks from heavy use are standard. Branding (if present) is minimal stamped text on chest or hem.
physical_description.closures: Single drawstring hood pulled tight at the crown. No other closures—the garment simply pulls on overhead. Slash pockets have no zippers or snaps, relying on design geometry to stay mostly watertight.
distinctive_features: Heat-welded seams instead of stitching—more durable, visible as raised ridges
Folds into its own compact pouch for transit storage
Two slash pockets positioned at waist, sized for tools, ration packs, or data-chip carriers
Drawstring hood with metal or plastic cord-locks
Crown opening reinforced to prevent tearing
Micro-brand stamps (Greycoast, Dura-Lo, Westpont Basics) often faded or partially illegible
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5. This is working-poor and sub-grade equipment. No corpo would wear it unless deep undercover. It signals economic precarity, transit dependency, and Shelf origin.
physical_description.cultural_context: Shelf dweller, transit worker, refugee, or anyone living in the ungoverned zones of the GLMZ. Wearing one announces you're used to weather, don't have access to climate-controlled spaces, and need waterproofing more than aesthetics. Also worn by corpo field teams doing intentional slumming.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn examples show weathered seams, micro-cracking along folds, faded color, and accumulated dirt in the heat-sealed ridge-lines. Some show small patches where the material has split. The drawstring cord frays. Despite this, they remain functional—the design is built for abuse.
